title: Commitment Fractionalizer and Supply Hysteresis: fractional reservations + cross-zone supply allocator
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduces fractional reservation sizing for Dedicated commitments (beta) and a supply hysteresis allocator to reduce cross-zone thrash; telemetry adds per-tenant effective utilization and aged-supply metrics.
description:
Motivation: customers with mixed steady and spiky workloads want more granular committed capacity without committing to full GPU units. This PR introduces a Commitment Fractionalizer that lets Dedicated commitments be expressed in fractional units (e.g., 0.25 of a slot) and a Supply Hysteresis Allocator that smooths cross-zone rebalances to avoid cascading preemptions. This change is gated behind a rollout flag (dedicated.fractional-commitments) and designed to be conservative by default.

What this PR does: 1) Adds a fractionalized commitment model on the reservation ledger and allocator: commitments are stored as fixed-point milli-slots to preserve determinism; admission, headroom and burst accounting are adapted to factor fractional reservations; 2) Implements a supply hysteresis layer in the inter-zone allocator that requires a delta threshold and a minimum stable window before moving fractional supply between zones; 3) Enhances telemetry: new metrics tenant_fractional_committed_{milli_slots}, tenant_effective_utilization_mavg_1m/5m/15m, and supply_age_seconds to reason about aged warm capacity; 4) Introduces a fairness tweak where fractional commitments are rounded only at execution time to nearest device slice to avoid starving tiny tenants; 5) Adds migration tool to convert existing integer commitments to milli-slot representation with a rollback path.

Compatibility and safety: - The fractional model is backwards compatible; integer commitments continue to be honored. - Rollout is opt-in per-cluster via feature flag. - Autoscaler and accounting paths include conservative checks: any bucketed admission that would reduce previously observed headroom below safety thresholds is disallowed. - Extensive unit tests and an integration job simulate mixed workloads (steady batch + microbursts) to verify no SLO regressions.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc (Linear ENG-4492) linked - [x] Unit & integration tests added - [x] Telemetry dashboards updated (grafana/dashboard id: cft-commit-fractionalizer) - [x] Feature flag gating - [x] Migration + rollback tooling - [x] Perf benchmarks (50k requests/min mixed load)

Related work: builds on prior autoscaler headroom work (ENG-4111) and the supply decay sampler (PR pr-41237). See perf notes in commits.

How to test locally: 1) enable feature flag dedicated.fractional-commitments=true in dev cluster; 2) run ./devctl alloc simulate --tenants 60 --fractional=true; 3) observe tenant_effective_utilization_* metrics and supply_age_seconds; 4) run migration tool: ./tools/migrate-commitments --dry-run.

Rollout plan: 1) Canary on staging with 10% traffic ~48h; 2) Monitor 95th/99th latency, token cost per-tenant and eviction counts; 3) Gradual 10% -> 50% -> 100% over two weeks only when eviction delta < 3% vs baseline.

Risks and mitigation: - Fractional rounding could cause micro-preemptions: mitigated by executing rounding at allocation time and by supply hysteresis window. - Accounting drift: added conversion & verification job. - Performance cost: fixed-point math is optimized and covered by benchmarks; no meaningful CPU-added overhead observed in 95th percentile under load test.

review_comments: Diego Morales: Please confirm rounding semantics when multiple fractional commitments exceed a single device slice — should we maintain FIFO or proportional assignment?
Maya Patel (author): We chose proportional assignment with deterministic tie-break by tenant id; added comment in fractional_admission.go and tests for saturation scenarios.
Renee Chen: CI failed initially on integration due to time-sensitive flakiness in the stable-window test. Could you add a backoff?
Maya Patel (author): Added exponential backoff and extended the stable-window to 5s in the test; CI re-run passed.
Arjun Singh: Suggest exposing supply_age_seconds with histogram buckets to help detect both very young and very stale supply — done.
SRE: Can we add an alert for supply_age_seconds > 600s in staging? Work item created SUP-9821.
Release Manager: Ensure migration tool logs are retained for 30 days; added retention flag and docs note.
